conventions.convention: Use a fixed oriented, time-oriented inertial Minkowski chart with metric diag(-1,1,1,1). Coordinates have length units; momenta and μ have inverse-length units. μ ≥ 0 is a mathematical parameter without a physical rest-mass identification.
The future shell has p⁰ > 0, ωμ(k) = sqrt(|k|² + μ²), and measure d³k/((2π)³ 2ωμ(k)). The massless apex is omitted and carries no point mass.
The phase is p∘x = p⁰x⁰ − p·x = −η(p,x). Kμf is the integral of f(x) exp(ip∘x), without a prefactor; the inverse full Fourier transform has prefactor (2π)^−4.

The Hilbert pairing is second-variable-linear. The complex-linear scalar field on D_fin is Φμ(f) = a(Kμ conjugate(f)) + a†(Kμf). For real f its closure is sqrt(2) times the Segal field at Kμf, and Wμ(f) = W_Segal(sqrt(2)Kμf).
The Poincare product is (a,Λ)(b,Γ) = (a + Λb, ΛΓ), with test action f_g(x) = f(Λ^−1(x − a)) and one-particle action Uμ(g)h(p) = exp(ip∘a)h(Λ^−1p).
Δμ has spatial Fourier multiplier sin(ωμt)/ωμ, initial time derivative δ₀, and scalar field commutator −iΔμ(f,g)I. The closed causal cone includes its boundary and origin.

Local scalar algebras are unital operator-norm closures generated by bounded Weyl operators for real compact smooth tests in arbitrary open regions. Spacelike separation means every pairwise difference is spacelike.
Countable Choice is assumed throughout the assigned construction and results.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, define Hμ = L²(Hμ⁺,dνμ;C), with μ ≥ 0, future shell p⁰ > 0, dνμ = d³k/((2π)³ 2ωμ(k)), and Kμf(p) = ∫f(x)exp(ip∘x)d⁴x for Schwartz f; omit the massless apex.

Assume Countable Choice and μ ≥ 0. Φμ(f) = a(Kμ conjugate(f)) + a†(Kμf) is a complex-linear weak operator-valued tempered distribution on D_fin, with restricted adjoint Φμ(conjugate(f)), vacuum covariance ⟨Kμ conjugate(f),Kμg⟩₂, positive normalized polynomial vacuum state, scalar Weyl phase exp(−i Im⟨Kμf,Kμg⟩₂), Poincare covariance, and translation spectral support in the closed future cone.

Assume Countable Choice. For μ ≥ 0, the tempered distribution Δμ with spatial Fourier multiplier sin(ωμt)/ωμ is supported in t² − |x|² ≥ 0. For real compact smooth f,g, [Φμ(f),Φμ(g)] = −iΔμ(f,g)I on D_fin; spacelike-separated supports give commuting fields.

Assume Countable Choice. For every μ ≥ 0, dνμ is locally finite and sigma-finite on Hμ⁺, and ∫g(Λ^−1p)dνμ(p) = ∫g(p)dνμ(p) for every proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation Λ and every nonnegative Borel shell function g.

Assume Countable Choice. For every μ ≥ 0, Hμ is separable and the Schwartz restriction range is dense in Hμ. The range contains every C_c∞(R³) chart function if μ > 0 and every C_c∞(R³ minus {0}) chart function if μ = 0.
Assume Countable Choice. For every μ ≥ 0, Kμ maps Schwartz space continuously and linearly into Hμ and satisfies Kμ((∂₀² − Δ + μ²)f) = 0 for every Schwartz f.

Assume Countable Choice. A unitary U:H→K lifts to a unitary Γ_s(U) between bosonic Fock spaces, preserving vacuum and finite-particle domains and intertwining creation and annihilation there. Strong continuity of a family of one-particle unitaries lifts to strong continuity on Fock space.

Assume Countable Choice. With the stated product topology and group law, Uμ(a,Λ)h(p) = exp(ip∘a)h(Λ^−1p) is a well-defined strongly continuous unitary representation, affine pullback preserves Schwartz space, and Kμf_g = Uμ(g)Kμf.

Assume Countable Choice. The unital norm-closed scalar Weyl algebras satisfy isotony for open-region inclusion and elementwise commutativity when every difference between the two open regions is spacelike. The generator of t↦Wμ(tf) is the closure of the real scalar field.

alerts.finding: The Statement says, “For each fixed coordinate time t in seconds,” while directly using the equal-time field Ψ_t(u) defined in lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality. That field uses W_D(t,k), whose defining supplier def-qft-dirac-projections explicitly makes t a “length-coordinate increment”; its phase is ωt with ω in inverse-length units. The physical theorem itself specifies x⁰ = ct. It does not state the corresponding Ψ_ct(u) conversion in this clause. The time label therefore has inconsistent declared units, although the norm-divergence argument is independent of the chosen fixed time.

seams_checked.note: Opened the Fock/test definition, CCR/CAR lemma, Segal/Weyl lemma and second-quantized spectrum lemma. The assigned consumers preserve second-variable linearity, separability where required, Countable Choice, finite-particle operator domains and exact generator domains. The scalar sqrt(2) rescaling correctly transfers the Segal Weyl phase and vacuum Gaussian. Draft suppliers remain explicitly conditional.

The observable-domain theorem cites bounded scalar local-algebra commutativity for exactly the supplier's open spacelike-separated regions. The correspondence theorem uses Klein–Gordon annihilation with the correct overall sign and applies the field formula to both f and its conjugate. Conditional model status and absence of empirical outcomes are retained. The separate time-unit presentation alert concerns its Dirac input.

The conformal theorem uses the massless field, shell phase, measure and bilinear covariance exactly as supplied. Smooth positive Ω sends compact tests to compact tests by multiplication with Ω³; continuity and the tested wave equation are proved locally. Complex-test locality is explicitly derived by splitting into real and imaginary parts, so the real-test causal supplier is not overstated.

The Dirac definition retains the metric, length coordinates, inverse-length dispersion and mathematical μ interpretation. Its locality lemma uses R = ∂τΔμ I₄ − i h_D(−i∇)Δμ and differential-support preservation with the correct scalar Δμ normalization. Its covariance lemma uses the exact invariant future-shell measure; the massless projection value at k = 0 affects only a Lebesgue-null point.
